title: The bee (I.3)
hook: devotion suits every vocation, like a bee takes honey without harming the flower
tomorrow: do you need a guide, or is God enough?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Philothea: a soul that loves God, living out in the world like a pearl in salt water. The line was for people in the world.

A new habit can wreck a life. The morning workout that makes you late for everyone else, the diet the whole house has to eat. So how do you add something to a life without wrecking it? Francis de Sales has a strange answer. In chapter three he lists three people trying hard to be holy: a bishop who lives alone in silence like a monk, a married person who wants to own nothing like a friar, a worker who stays in church all day. And he calls all three ridiculous. Why would a saint say that?
screen: `A NEW HABIT CAN WRECK A LIFE.` → `THREE PEOPLE TRYING TO BE HOLY.` → `HE CALLS THEM RIDICULOUS.`

segments.voice: Because their devotion doesn't fit their lives. At creation, de Sales recalls, God told the plants to bear fruit each after its kind. In the same way, he says, devotion is meant to be lived by each person according to their state: the worker, the servant, the ruler, the widow, the young, the married. The bishop has a diocese to care for. The married person has a household. The worker has work that's going undone. Devotion that wrecks a calling is out of order. Then the picture that solves the puzzle. He borrows a line he credits to Aristotle: the bee takes honey from flowers without harming them, and leaves them as whole and fresh as it found them. True devotion, de Sales says, does even better. It spoils no calling. It makes each one more beautiful. Here's one for tonight: he says precious stones dipped in honey shine brighter, each in its own color. So the answer to the hook: add devotion the way a bee visits a flower. If the family, the team or the job is worse off, something's out of order. If they're brighter, that's honey.
screen: `EACH AFTER ITS KIND.` · `DEVOTION THAT WRECKS IS OUT OF ORDER.` · `THE BEE LEAVES THE FLOWER WHOLE.` · `STONES IN HONEY SHINE BRIGHTER.` · then, large: `HONEY WITHOUT HARM.`

segments.voice: Pick one small task you'll do today, a shift, a set of dishes, a homework problem, a diaper. Picture doing it slowly and well, leaving the people around it better off than you found them. Then do one tiny piece of it with that care right now, even straightening one thing within reach.
The bee. De Sales's picture of devotion: it draws honey from every calling and harms none, leaving each one brighter.
Carry this: honey without harm, devotion that leaves the flower whole and the work brighter. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics speak of holiness in one's state of life: married people, workers, students, priests and religious each live devotion in a different way, a theme the Church took up strongly in the Second Vatican Council's universal call to holiness.

chat.meaning: The bee takes honey without harming the flower. Devotion should fit your state, team captain included, and leave it better.

Francis de Sales.meaning: a bishop and writer, author of the Introduction to the Devout Life

friar.meaning: a member of a religious order who owns nothing personally

diocese.meaning: the area and people a bishop cares for

sources.ref: Introduction to the Devout Life I.3

notes: Introduction I.3 paraphrased: God commanded the plants to bring forth fruit each according to its kind; so devotion is to be practiced differently by the gentleman, the worker, the servant, the prince, the widow, the maid, the married; a bishop wanting to live as a Carthusian, a married person owning nothing like a Capuchin, a worker always in church: such devotion would be ridiculous, disorderly and intolerable; the bee (Aristotle) draws honey without hurting flowers; devotion does better, spoiling no vocation but adorning it; precious stones dipped in honey grow brighter, each in its own color. 'A monk' and 'a friar' stand for Carthusian and Capuchin. Confirm.
howItsDone: Vatican II's universal call to holiness (Lumen Gentium ch. 5) named as a theme; confirm framing.
